- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged decline; reduce forecast slope to avoid overshoot.  
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75), model often fails to recognize it; add a 2–5% upward bias to forecast to counteract downward drift.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price drops after sentiment shifts to negative; apply a 1–2% upward adjustment to forecast if sentiment turns negative.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.00, 0.00, 1.00), model may misread trend; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
